findings.description: The wrapper now clears and reuses one shared statistics dict on every call to the decorated function. Concurrent or nested/recursive calls of the same wrapped function therefore share and mutate the same dict.
findings.rationale: Trigger: the same decorated function runs in two threads, or recursively. The second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's in-progress counters, and both calls then write into the same dict. Impact: attempt_number, idle_for and the other statistics are corrupted. The old code created a fresh dict per call via copy.statistics, and the comment above this hunk says the copy exists to avoid exactly this overwriting.

findings.description: The async wrapper clears and reuses a single shared statistics dict for every call. Concurrent coroutines running the same decorated function overwrite each other's statistics.
findings.rationale: Trigger: asyncio.gather over several calls of the same @retry-decorated coroutine function. Each call starts with stats.clear() and then writes into the same dict. Impact: the statistics mix across the calls and are wrong. The previous per-call copy.statistics kept them separate.
